newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees closing deal with London Club end '97.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees closing deal with London Club end '97.

text.p: Russia may close an agreement with the London Club of commercial bank-creditors by the end of 1997, Vneshekonombank, the state agent on foreign debt, said on Wednesday after a meeting between London Club officials and the Russian government.

"During the talks in was noted that the current dynamics of the reconciliation process and preparation of the necessary documents will allow us to close the London Club deal by the end of the year," Vneshekonombank said in a statement.
Vneshekonombank said the volume of fully reconciled debt amounted to two-thirds of eligible debt.

Earlier, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov had said the reconciled debt volume was close to 65 percent of the $24 billion principle debt. Russia's total debt, inherited from the former Soviet Union, is $35 billion.
To close the London Club deal, Russia has to reconcile 90 percent of the principle debt.
